texts.facts: Sumit information was received at PS Adarsh Nagar, vide GD No. 043A to the effect that the "Caller Ko Kisi Ne Goli Mar Di He", which was assigned to ASI Sanjeev, who along with his staff reached at the spot, but by that time the injured had already been shifted to BJRM Hospital by PCR. In the meantime, IO SI Satwant Singh along with Ct. Pradeep also reached at the spot. IO SI Satwant, leaving ASI Sanjeev at the spot, left for BJRM Hospital and found the injured Harish Chander under medical treatment and unfit for statement. IO SI Satwant Singh collected the MLC of injured and considering the nature of injuries sustained by the injured, he prepared the rukka and got the FIR registered through Ct. Pradeep. On 27.08.2019, IO SI Satwant Singh recorded the statement of injured, wherein he complained that accused Sumit along with his mother resides in his neighbourhood and he knew them for the last about 8-10 years. About three years back, the complainant had lent Rs. 1,76,000/- to the mother of accused, qua which the accused and his mother used to pay him Rs. 8000/- per month towards interest. For the last about two months prior to the incident, the accused was avoiding to pay the interest. Complainant further complained that on 26.08.2019 at about 11.00 AM, when he Nisha Sahay was present outside his clinic, accused along with associate V Saxena SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit @ B (CCL) went to the house adjacent to his clinic and after about 5-7 minutes, the accused Sumit and his associate V @ B (CCL) came to him and said "Byaj Ke Rupay Hamesha Ke Liye Bhool Ja. Aaj Tera Kaam Tamaam Kar Dete Hain" (Forget about the interest money forever. I will finish your work today). Accused Sumit fired a gun shot from a country made pistol on left side of his abdomen. Thereafter, accused also hit him on his head with butt of the said country made pistol, and ran away. The injured called the police at 100 number, pursuant whereto he was removed to BJRM Hospital by PCR. 3. During investigation, the accused Sumit was apprehended and arrested by SI Satwant, who recorded his disclosure statement. Since the associate of accused Sumit, was found 16 years of age (CCL), the requisite proceedings were conducted qua him. Subsequently, accused Sumit and CCL V @ B got recovered the weapon of offence i.e. country made pistol from Ganda Naala, near Jailer wala Bagh, Azadpur, Delhi. Upon completion of the investigation, charge-sheet was filed against the accused, and after cognizance was taken by the Ld. Magistrate, the case was committed to the Sessions Court for trial. Charge was framed against the accused Sumit for offences punishable under Section 307 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and under Section 25/27 Arms Act. The accused pleaded not guilty to charge and claimed trial. 21. PW 21 SI Virender Filed supplementary charge-sheet Kumar qua Sanction u/s 39 Arms Act and FSL result. True copy of DD No.43 Ex.PW3/A 6. In his statement under Section 313 CrPC, the accused Sumit denied all the allegations and claimed false implication by the police. In support of his defence, the accused examined Nisha Sahay Saxena SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit Smt. Seema as DW 1 and Sh. Manoj Singh as DW 2, to prove that he was not even present at the time of alleged incident. The case of the prosecution is to the effect that on the fateful day i.e. 26.08.2019, accused Sumit accompanied by his associate V @ B, fired gun shot on the left side of the abdomen of injured Harish Chander with a country made pistol and also hit him on his head with the butt of the said country made pistol. The motive assigned to the accused for causing injuries to the injured is to the effect that he did not want to pay the interest on the loan amount of Rs. 1,76,000/- taken by his mother from the injured. OFFENCE U/S 307 IPC 9. The accused has been charged for the offence punishable u/s 307 IPC. Some persons had gathered at the spot and they all took Sh. Harish Chander to the clinic and informed the PCR about the incident by dialing 100 number. PCR van accordingly reached the spot and took Sh. Harish Chander to hospital. He further deposed that Sh. Harish Chander had left the clinic on hearing the noise, which was coming from near the temple. Sh. Harish Chander had informed him that PCR call was made. He volunteered that after the incident, he tried to chase the accused Sumit and when he returned to the spot, Sh. Harish Chander had informed him in this regard. The statement of Sh. Harish Chander was not recorded by PCR officials in his clinic as he was not in a position to make the statement due to the injuries. Sh. Harish Chander was in conscious condition when he was taken to hospital. He had not informed to the family members Nisha Sahay of Sh. Harish Chander as he was not having phone number of Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 13 of 39 Date: SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit wife of Sh. Harish Chander. Family members of Sh. Harish Chander had reached the clinic in his presence. Wife of Sh. Harish Chander had also visited the hospital. He remained in the hospital till evening. 14. PW 2 further deposed that he had stated to the IO that Sh. Harish Chander had left the clinic on hearing the noise which was coming from near the temple. He was confronted with his statement Ex. PW2/DA, where the above said fact was not found so recorded. He further deposed that he had seen the IO in the hospital but no inquiry was made by the IO from him in the hospital. He also did not try to talk to the IO in the hospital narrating the facts of the incident in question. He denied the suggestion that he did not meet the IO in the hospital as he was not present in the hospital at that time. He admitted it to be correct that Sh. Harish Chander used to deal in the business of finance as well. He denied the suggestion that the accused Sumit had not caused any injuries to Sh. Harish Chander in his presence. 15. Sumit tera kaam tamam kar dete hain " and thereafter accused Sumit (correctly identified) fired upon him with a Katta, due to which he received bullet injury on the lower side of his stomach. He fell down and then accused Sumit alongwith his associate V (CCL) gave injuries to him with the butt of the katta. He further deposed that thereafter, he made a PCR call by dialing 100 number, pursuant whereto PCR came and took him to BJRM Hospital and from the said hospital he was referred to LNJP Hospital, where he had to remain admitted for about 4/5 days. 16. PW 4 Harish Chander further deposed that accused Sumit resides in his locality and he had given cash amount of Rs. 1,76,000/- to the mother of accused Sumit about 3 years back from the date of incident. Accused Sumit used to pay the interest of Rs. 6,000/- per month for the above said amount to him, but about 2-3 months prior to the date of the incident, accused Sumit had not come to pay the said monthly interest to him and on being asked to pay the same, accused Sumit would linger on the matter on one pretext or the other. PW 4 correctly identified the country made pistol, produced by MHC(M), as the same with which accused Sumit had fired upon him, as Ex.P1. He also State vs Sumit on 14 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175330920/ 9 identified his pants with belt, one underwear, one blood stained baniyan and one blood stained shirt, worn by Nisha him at the time of incident, as Ex.P2 (colly). In his cross examination by Ld. defence counsel, he admitted it to be correct that he had no document to show that he is a RMP. However, he brought on record the photocopy of Certificate of Completion dated 02.04.2018 in Herbal Nutrition issued by Vice President and Country Head, India, of Herbalife Nutrition, as Mark PW4/X-1. He also brought on record the original Registration Certificate issued by Department of Food Safety, Delhi Government, in his favour as Ex. PW4/X-2. He admitted it to be correct that the said Certificate only authorized him to carry on the food businesses and not for any other purpose. He admitted it to be correct that he was unable to produce any document pertaining to his qualification being RMP Doctor. 18. PW 4 Harish Chander further deposed that he had opened his clinic on 26.08.2019 at about 10:30 am. There was no compounder / helper working with him in his clinic. He knew the accused previously because he was residing in his neighbourhood in the same building. He had given, in cash, an amount of Rs. 1,76,000/- (Rupees one lakh seventy six thousand only) to the mother of accused, but he did not know the date when he had given the said amount to the mother of Nisha accused. He volunteered that an agreement had taken place Sahay Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 16 of 39 Saxena SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit between him, Amit (brother of accused Sumit as disclosed by DW1) and the mother of accused and a civil case is also pending in the Court in this regard. He further deposed that his family had sold the garden / field of mango trees in their native village and the said cash amount was the part of sale proceeds of the said transaction. Cash amount of Rs.1,76,000/- was in his possession, which he had given to the mother of the accused. He had no documentary proof to show that he had sold the garden/field of mango trees in his native place. He did not issue any receipt to the accused regarding receipt of interest amount of Rs. 6000/- per month. He denied the suggestion that he did not issue any receipt in this regard as no such transaction had ever taken place between him and the mother of the accused. He did not issue any notice to the accused demanding interest on the said amount given by him to the mother of the accused.
texts.arguments: For ready reference, Section 307 IPC is being reproduced herein below : 307. Attempt to murder.--Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such Nisha Sahay Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 8 of 39 by Nisha Sahay SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years and shall also be liable to fine; and if hurt is caused to any person by such act, the offender shall be liable either to imprisonment for life, or to such punishment as is hereinbefore mentioned. Intention - "Criminal intention" simply means the purpose or design of doing an act forbidden by the criminal law without just cause or excuse. As a Sahay Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 9 of 39 Saxena SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit general rule, every sane man is presumed to intend the necessary or the natural and probable consequences of his acts, and this presumption of law will prevail unless from a consideration of all the evidence the court entertains a reasonable doubt whether such intention existed. This presumption, however, is not conclusive nor alone sufficient to justify a conviction and should be supplemented by other testimony. An accused must be judged to have the intention that is indicated by his proved acts. Knowledge - Motive may Sahay Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 10 of 39 by Nisha Sahay SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit serve as a clue to the intention; but although the motive be pure, the act done under it may be criminal. Purity of motive does not purge an act of its criminal character. An act which is unlawful cannot, in law, be excused on the ground that it was committed from a good motive. But in cases of circumstantial Sahay Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 11 of 39 Nisha Sahay Saxena SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit evidence, absence of motive is a factor in favour of the accused. Act. He denied the suggestion that he had not mentioned these facts in the case u/s 138 of N.I. Act because no such incident/firing had taken place. He further deposed that he had not disclosed the name of the accused to the Doctor in the hospital, who had prepared his MLC. He had disclosed the name of the person, who had fired upon him, in the PCR call made by him at 100 number. He admitted it to be correct that the name of accused / any other person is not mentioned in DD No. 043-A. He further admitted it to be correct that the site plan does not bear his signature. 21. The star witnesses of the prosecution is the injured himself and he fits the bill of a sterling witness. The injured is Nisha Sahay the star and sterling witness of the prosecution and stood the Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 18 of 39 Saxena SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit test of a grilling cross-examination. In Rai Sandeep Vs. State (NCT of Delhi) (2012) 8 SCC 21, Hon'ble Apex Court observed as under : "In our considered opinion, the 'sterling witness' should be of a very high quality and caliber whose version should, therefore, be unassailable. The Court considering the version of such witness should be in a position to accept it for its face value without any hesitation. To test the quality of such a witness, the status of the witness would be immaterial and what would be relevant is the truthfulness of the statement made by such a witness. It should be natural and consistent with the case of the prosecution qua the accused. 22. Ld. counsel for accused has argued that there are material contradictions in the testimony of two material witnesses examined by the prosecution, which go to the root of the matter and create reasonable doubt on the prosecution version. However, it is to be noted that Nisha Sahay Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 20 of 39 Nisha Sahay SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit PW 4 in his cross examination has categorically deposed that at the relevant time, his nephew was present in the clinic. 23. Ld. defence counsel has further argued that as per the version of PW 2 Manoj, at the relevant time he along with his uncle Harish Chander was present in the clinic, and on hearing some noise, his uncle Harish Chander went outside and after sometime on hearing the noise of firing, he (PW 2) also went outside. On the other hand, on this aspect, the version of PW 4 Harish Chander is that at the relevant time, he was standing in front of Balmiki Mandir, which was situated in front of his clinic, when accused Sumit accompanied by his associate V @ B approached him and caused him alleged gun shot injury and butt blow injury. 24. Ld. defence counsel has further argued that the accused Sumit and V@ B (CCL) were already known to the injured but in his first call to the PCR, injured has only informed that someone had fired upon him. It is submitted that had the injured actually been shot by the accused Sumit, the injured must have named the accused in his first call to the police. It is further submitted that PW 4 in his cross examination deposed that he had disclosed the name of the person, who had fired upon him, in the PCR call made by him at 100 number, but on being confronted with DD No. 43 A, Nisha Sahay Saxena FIR No Such minor contradictions do not prove fatal to the prosecution case, as the fact remains that the injured Nisha sustained gun shot injury and the question to be adjudicated Sahay Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 23 of 39 Saxena SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit upon is as to whether the said injury was caused by the accused or not. 26. To understand the weight which is to be given to the deposition of witnesses, guidance needs to be taken from the Hon'ble Superior Courts. In State of Rajasthan v. Smt. Kalki & Anr., 1981 SCC (2) 752, it was held as under: "In the depositions of witnesses there are always some normal discrepancies however honest and truthful they may be. These discrepancies are due to normal errors of observation, normal errors of memory due to lapse of time, due to mental disposition such as shock and horror at the time of the occurrence, and the like. Material discrepancies are those which are not normal, and not expected of a normal person." 27. In Raj Kumar Singh @ Raju @ Batya v. State of Rajasthan (2013) 5 SCC 722, it was observed as under: "It is a settled legal proposition that, while appreciating the evidence of a witness, minor discrepancies on trivial matters, which do not affect the core of the case of the prosecution, must not prompt the court to reject the evidence thus provided, in its entirety. The irrelevant details which do not in any way corrode the credibility of a witness, cannot be labeled as omissions or contradictions. Therefore, the courts must be cautious and very particular, in their exercise of appreciating evidence. The approach to be adopted is, if the evidence of a witness is read in its entirety, and the same appears to have in it, a ring Nisha Sahay of truth, then it may become necessary for the court to Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 24 of 39 Date: State vs Sumit on 14 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175330920/ 13 SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit scrutinize the evidence more particularly, keeping in mind the deficiencies, drawbacks and infirmities pointed out in the said evidence as a whole, and evaluate them separately, to determine whether the same are completely against the nature of the evidence provided by the witnesses, and whether the validity of such evidence is shaken by virtue of such evaluation, rendering it unworthy of belief." 28. It is to be kept in mind that in Bhagwan Jagannath Markad & ors. Vs. State of Maharashtra, (2016) 10 SCC 537 and Maqsoodan Vs. State of UP, (1983) 1 SCC 2018 , the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that presence of the injured witness at the time and place of occurrence cannot be doubted and the fact that he had received injuries during the course of incident, in normal course should not be doubted and disbelieved. 17:23:59 +0530 SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit 30. In case Abdul Sayed V. State of MP, (2010) 10 SCC 259, to explain the reliability of injured witnesses, it was held that "Where witness to occurrence was himself injured State vs Sumit on 14 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175330920/ 14 Nisha Sahay in the incident, testimony of such witness is Saxena generally considered to be very reliable, as he is a Digitally signed by Nisha Sahay Saxena Date: 2025.11.14 17:24:04 +0530 SC No. 116/2021 State Vs witness that comes with an inbuilt guarantee of his presence at the scene of crime and is unlikely to spare his actual assailant (s) in order to falsely implicate someone 38. Ld. counsel for accused has argued that the recovery of weapon of offence has not been proved as per the standard of proof required, in as much as the handkerchief which was used by the IO for cleaning the country made pistol was not seized by the IO, the site plan of the place of recovery was not prepared and that the Crime Team was not called at the place of recovery. State vs Sumit on 14 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175330920/ 15 39. It is to be noted that the said handkerchief, which was used by the IO to clear the country made pistol, belonged to the IO and was not the case property and hence did not require to be seized. Ld. defence counsel has also argued that no public person was joined in investigation at the time of recovery of country made pistol. PW 16 IO SI Satwant Singh, corroborated by his staff / police officials, who accompanied him at the time of recovery of weapon, has categorically deposed that since no one was present at the relevant time, no one was joined in the investigation. 40. Further more, it is settled law that for want of public / independent witnesses, prosecution case cannot be rejected. I place reliance upon Ambika Prasad Vs. State (Delhi Nisha Sahay Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 29 of 39 Digitally signed by Nisha Sahay Saxena Date: 2025.11.14 17:24:25 +0530 SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit Administration), 2000 (2) SCC 646, wherein it was observed that "It is known fact that independent persons are reluctant to be a witness or assist the investigation. The attitude of the public in the investigation of crimes is indifferent. Nor is it proper to reject the case for want of corroboration by independent witnesses if the case made out is otherwise true and acceptable." 41. 42. Ld. defence counsel has further argued that as per Nisha Sahay Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 30 of 39 by Nisha Sahay SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit the prosecution case, the weapon of offence i.e. country made pistol was recovered from Ganda Nala and at the time of recovery, the pistol was without any cover or polythene bag and that the same was smeared in mud, and as such the same would not be functional. However, as per the FSL report, the pistol was found functional. The contention of Ld. defence counsel that since the pistol was smeared in mud the same would not function, does not seem justified as the country made pistol remained in mud for a short span of time and further it depends upon the quality of the mechanical device. 46. Ld. defence counsel has argued that there are various lapses in the investigation carried out by the concerned police officials and contradictions in the testimony of police witnesses. Similar approach was reiterated by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case Paras Yadav V. State of Bihar (Jan 12, 1999), that minor flaws in the investigation would not automatically invalidate a prosecution case if the core evidence is reliable. Poor investigation alone cannot be the reason for acquittal if injured witness' testimony establishes guilt beyond reasonable doubt. It may be noted in this regard that relevant part of section 3(1) of Arms Act states that no person shall acquire, have in his State vs Sumit on 14 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175330920/ 18 possession, or carry any firearm or ammunition unless he holds in this behalf a licence issued in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the rules made there under. 54. The first pre-condition for an offence under Section 25(1) (a) is the element of intention, consciousness or knowledge with which a person possessed the firearm before it can be said to constitute an offence and secondly that possession need not be physical possession but can be constructive, having power and control over the gun, while the person to whom physical possession is given holds it subject to that power and control. It may also be noted that section 27(1) of the Arms Act mandates that whoever, inter alia, uses any arms or ammunition in contravention of section 5 shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine. Further it may also be noted that section 5(1) of Arms Act states that no person shall use, manufacture, sell, transfer, convert, repair, test or prove, or expose or offer for sale or transfer or have in his possession for sale, transfer, conversion, repair, test or proof, any firearm or any other arms of such class or description as may be Nisha Sahay prescribed or any ammunition, unless he holds in this behalf a Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 38 of 39 17:25:15 +0530 SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit licence issued in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder.

Intention - "Criminal intention" simply means the purpose or design of doing an act forbidden by the criminal law without just cause or excuse. As a Sahay Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 9 of 39 Saxena SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit general rule, every sane man is presumed to intend the necessary or the natural and probable consequences of his acts, and this presumption of law will prevail unless from a consideration of all the evidence the court entertains a reasonable doubt whether such intention existed. This presumption, however, is not conclusive nor alone sufficient to justify a conviction and should be supplemented by other testimony. An accused must be judged to have the intention that is indicated by his proved acts. Knowledge - Motive may Sahay Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 10 of 39 by Nisha Sahay SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit serve as a clue to the intention; but although the motive be pure, the act done under it may be criminal. Purity of motive does not purge an act of its criminal character. An act which is unlawful cannot, in law, be excused on the ground that it was committed from a good motive. But in cases of circumstantial Sahay Saxena FIR No. 285/2019 : PS Adarsh Nagar Page 11 of 39 Nisha Sahay Saxena SC No. 116/2021 State Vs. Sumit evidence, absence of motive is a factor in favour of the accused. In Rai Sandeep Vs. To test the quality of such a witness, the status of the witness would be immaterial and what would be relevant is the truthfulness of the statement made by such a witness. It should be natural and consistent with the case of the prosecution qua the accused. In State of Rajasthan v. Smt. Kalki & Anr., 1981 SCC (2) 752, it was held as under: "In the depositions of witnesses there are always some normal discrepancies however honest and truthful they may be. These discrepancies are due to normal errors of observation, normal errors of memory due to lapse of time, due to mental disposition such as shock and horror at the time of the occurrence, and the like. Material discrepancies are those which are not normal, and not expected of a normal person." 27. In Raj Kumar Singh @ Raju @ Batya v.
